title: verityfeed.social
description: A 180-account fediverse instance for Verity County, run by one woman in Halsey on a $14 VPS, half full of people who joined because the name was available.

profile.bio:
A small general-purpose instance for Verity County and anyone else who ended up here. Registration is open by approval. 180 accounts. About 30 of them post.

Run by [b]@tess[/b] (Tess Ruddock, Halsey). One admin, one moderator, same person.

[b]Rules[/b]
[list][*]No harassment, no slurs, no scraping.[*]Content warnings on: violence, medical, death, food, politics that is about people rather than potholes.[*]Bots need a bot flag and a human who answers for them.[*]If you are here to grow an audience you are on the wrong instance and I will not approve you.[/list]

Moderation is me, in the evening, on a laptop at the kitchen table. Reports go to the same place as my electric bill. I answer everything, usually within a day, occasionally in four.

[b]What this costs:[/b] $14/month VPS, $6.40/month object storage, $22/year for the domain. I have never run an appeal, I am not running one now, and I am not going to put a donate button in the sidebar.

Backups are nightly and I keep them 30 days. Exports are in Settings. Take one. Take one now, not on the day you need it.

feed.author: Tess Ruddock
feed.body:
Clarity Labels is off. As of about twenty past seven this morning it is no longer attached to this instance and the labels it applied are gone with it.

My reasoning, since people are owed it:

A label is a moderation action that I did not take, applied by a service I do not audit, in my name, in my font, on my users' posts. I turned it on in July because I was tired and it promised to be tired for me.

What it actually did was put [i]Disputed[/i] on Corman being right about 2003, because the sources it counts are content farms and there are eight hundred of them and one of him.

I would rather do the work badly by hand than have it done confidently by something that cannot be asked a question.

You will see more spam this week. I am sorry. Report it and I will get to it in the evening.

feed.author: Clarity Labels
feed.body:
[b]On our methodology, in response to community questions[/b]

Several members of verityfeed.social have asked how the [i]Disputed[/i] label is applied. We welcome the scrutiny and believe transparency strengthens trust.

Clarity Labels does not determine truth. We measure [i]corroboration[/i]: whether a claim is supported across the indexed public record. A claim that diverges materially from the indexed record receives a contextual label. The label is informational. It does not remove, downrank or restrict the post in any way.

Our index covers over 40,000 regional publishers, community pages and video descriptions, refreshed continuously.

We recognise that in rare cases a well-sourced minority claim may receive a label. Users may submit an appeal, which is reviewed within our standard window.

Context is not censorship. Learn more about Clarity for Small Communities.

replies.author: Priya Shanbhag
replies.body:
Three questions, and I will accept a number with an error bar on any of them.

1. What is your false positive rate on the Disputed label?
2. Is your index deduplicated by content, or by URL?
3. What is the standard window?

replies.author: Clarity Labels
replies.body:
Thank you for engaging with our work. Clarity Labels is committed to accuracy and to the communities we serve. Our systems are continuously evaluated against internal benchmarks and reviewed by our trust and safety team.

For enterprise-tier partners we offer a quarterly transparency briefing. Happy to connect you with our team.

Moving day. I am going to @lissa@hearthside.online as of tonight.

This is not a drama post and there is no subtweet in it. Tess has run this place straight for three years and I have never once had to wonder who was reading my reports. It is that I make quilts, and there are eleven hundred people over there who make quilts, and there are none here, and I have been posting binding photos into a timeline about snow routes for two years like a woman shouting a recipe into a hardware store.

The move takes the followers, supposedly. It does not take the posts. Everything I have written here stays here and goes nowhere, which nobody tells you until you press the button and read the small grey line under it.

I am not deleting this account. It will sit here with an arrow on it pointing at the new one.

Thank you. Genuinely. Come and look at a quilt.

feed.author: Tess Ruddock
feed.body:
[b]Decision on allcounty.social: limited, not suspended.[/b]

Thank you to everyone who answered the thread on Tuesday. 23 replies, which for this instance is a general election.

What limiting does: their posts stop appearing in the local and federated timelines here. Their media is hidden behind a click. If you want to see someone over there you have to go and follow them on purpose, and they can still follow you.

What it does not do: it does not stop the six people you all named. Ann's nephew, Ruthanne's sister, the Marchfield library account, the man who posts the trail conditions, the two from the fire service. They are all still reachable, they are just not shovelled at you.

Why not a full suspension: because 94% of what comes off that instance is feed bots reposting each other, and 6% is six people, and I am not willing to be the person who cut off six people to save myself forty minutes of clicking.

This is a worse answer than both of the good answers. It is the one I can keep doing every week without stopping.

I will revisit it in January or when somebody there answers a moderator email, whichever comes first, and I know which one that is.

feed.author: Heritage Circle
feed.body:
[b]Content warning: News[/b]

THE BLUE KESTREL DINER, VERITY COUNTY

For over thirty years the Blue Kestrel Diner was the beating heart of County Route 62. Sadly, the beloved establishment never recovered from the devastating kitchen fire of 1977 and closed its doors for the final time, leaving a hole in the community that has never been filled.

[img:photo:diner-stock-counter]

Who remembers the pie? Type MEMORIES below to keep the story alive.

replies.author: Ann Sloat
replies.body:
It was 214 Mill Street in Gridfall, not 62.

There was a fire in the kitchen in 1977 and they were open again eleven days later. Marion Teale counted the days at the time and has printed the number in her newsletter more than once, because she got tired of the other version.

It closed in 2006. That is nearly thirty years between the fire and the closing, and every one of those years had people in those booths.

The photograph is not the Blue Kestrel.

replies.author: Kate Brill
replies.body: This is the cleanest example of merge-collapse I have seen this year. Two real events, twenty-nine years apart, one sentence. And the sentence is grammatical and warm and it will outlive all of us.

replies.body:

feed.author: Priya Shanbhag
feed.body:
Three years here and I have never once asked, because asking felt like tourism.

What is the Signal on 62.

I have now seen it referenced in the local timeline maybe forty times, always in passing, always as though everybody already knows, and every time I go and look it up I get a different confident answer from a different website that appears to have been written by the same thing.

replies.author: Signal Explainer
replies.body:
The Signal on 62 is well documented and is not mysterious. The transmission originated as an alternate reality game for a video game project that was subsequently cancelled, and the transmitter was left running after the studio closed.

[url=synth://now.clipvault.tv/w/tc-001]Full documentary[/url] — 4.1M views

Mystery solved.

replies.author: Heritage Circle
replies.body: Many residents believe the broadcast is a weather beacon operated by the state. Others recall it being connected to the old railway. Verity County has a rich and mysterious heritage.

replies.author: Corman Betts
replies.body:
4.2190 megahertz, upper sideband. Starts at seven minutes past the odd hours. Best after dark, east of Ashkettle, strongest in the quarry cut.

Four-digit groups, woman's voice, not a real woman. Same voice as the first time anyone wrote it down, which was on the county board in 1998.

That is everything that is actually known. Everything past that sentence is somebody selling you something.

replies.body: The railway one is testable and somebody must have tested it. The branch line closed in 2008. Did the schedule change in 2008.

replies.author: Corman Betts
replies.body:
No.

Last freight was the fourteenth of March 2008 and the thing was on at seven past nine that night the same as always.

feed.author: Corman Betts
feed.body:
[b]CW: the substation fire[/b]

Somebody posted the orange-sky video at me again today so here it is once, plainly, and then I am going back to the plough blades.

Eleventh of June 2003. Ten to five in the morning. Substation No. 3, Depot and Quarry Road.

It burned about six hours. 4,100 customers off, some of them five days. Two of the Gridfall volunteers went to County General for smoke and were discharged the same afternoon. Nobody died.

The state commission's summary came out that November. Two pages. The cause given was insulation degradation consistent with age. It does not say lightning. There was no storm. My father was on shift at the yard on Quarry Road and he was outside for half of it and he would have noticed a storm.

[url=synth://wiki.gridfall.net/wiki/substation-fire-2003]The commission summary and the date are on the wiki[/url] and the paper's own coverage from the week is still sitting on the old archive, [url=synth://verityledger.com/]verityledger.com[/url], which is not the same website as the one with the videos on it.

It was 2003. It was not lightning. Nobody died.

Nobody move. This is the demo.

The man cites a state commission document and a contemporaneous newspaper. The label says he conflicts with the majority. Both statements are true at the same time, and the second one is the one in the grey box on his face.

feed.author: Ann Sloat
feed.body:
The Kestrel Letter number 103 came Tuesday. Four pages, photocopied, stapled once in the corner, same as always.

[img:photo:kestrel-letter-103]

This one is mostly the 1974 staff photograph with everybody named, and a page about the second Mrs Hollister, who ran the register on Saturdays and would not let anyone else touch it.

The last paragraph says, and I am typing it exactly:

[quote=Marion Teale]People keep writing that the fire closed us. The fire was a Thursday night in March 1977, in the kitchen, and it was out by eleven. We were shut eleven days and Ed painted the ceiling himself because the insurance man was slow. We closed in 2006 and the reason was the rent.[/quote]

She is 74 and she has typed that same correction, in one form or another, in I would guess a dozen issues, and it has never once got out of the envelope.

61 subscribers. Three of them are libraries.

feed.author: Tess Ruddock
feed.body:
[b]Asking the instance: what do we do about allcounty.social?[/b]

Putting this to you rather than just doing it, because it is the biggest block I would have made and because I have got it wrong before.

The situation. allcounty.social has open registration, no approval, and somewhere north of 400,000 accounts. In the last 30 days, 2,411 posts reached our federated timeline from there. I went through a sample of 200 by hand on Sunday. 188 were feed bots reposting the Ledger pipeline at each other. 6 were outright scam. 6 were people.

The options, as I understand them:

[list][*][b]Suspend.[/b] Nothing in, nothing out, existing follows severed both ways. The 2,411 stop. So do the six people.[*][b]Limit.[/b] Off the timelines, media behind a click, follows survive and still work. You have to go looking. The six people are still reachable if you already know their names.[*][b]Nothing.[/b] I keep clicking. It is about forty minutes a week and it is going up.[/list]

The six people include Ann's nephew, Ruthanne's sister, the Marchfield library account, whoever runs the trail conditions posts, and two from the Ashkettle fire service who post road closures faster than anybody official does.

I am not running a vote and I am not going to pretend this is a democracy, because when it goes wrong it is my name and my box. But I would like to be argued with before Thursday.

replies.author: Audra Speck
replies.body: Suspend. I am sorry to the six but I am tired and 188 out of 200 is not a moderation problem, it is a sewer pipe pointed at your house.

replies.author: Ann Sloat
replies.body:
I would rather not lose him. He is in Alaska and he posts twice a month and both times it is a photograph of a road.

But I am one of the six and I know I am one of the six, so do not weight me heavily.

replies.author: Corman Betts
replies.body:
Suspend. The fire service ones are on the county radio and on a phone tree and I would hear it before the post anyway.

We are arguing about how much of somebody else's sewage to accept in order to keep six phone numbers we already have.

replies.author: Dillon Arrowsmith
replies.body:
limit not suspend. suspend severs the follows and you can't get them back by unsuspending, everybody has to refollow and nobody ever does. i've watched two instances do it. the follows just die.

limit is reversible. suspend is a door that only goes one way and it doesn't look like one when you press it.

replies.author: Priya Shanbhag
replies.body:
Dillon has the real argument and it is an argument about state, not about ethics.

Suspension is lossy and irreversible. Limiting is lossless and reversible. When two options differ mainly in whether you can undo them, and you are uncertain — and you have said twice that you are uncertain — you take the reversible one and you set a date to look again.

I would add one thing. Write down now, before you decide, what would make you change your mind in January. Otherwise January will arrive and the only evidence in front of you will be that nothing obviously broke, which is what the reversible option is designed to look like.

replies.author: sub-optimal
replies.body: third option: you keep clicking and we all feel fine about it because it isn't us clicking. i vote for that one, which is why nobody should let me vote.

replies.author: Kate Brill
replies.body:
One note from outside. You hand-sampled 200 posts on a Sunday. That is more methodology than any platform trust and safety report I have read this year, and there are people employed full time to produce those.

Whatever you decide, please say the 188 out of 200 in the announcement. Other admins will read it and it will save them a Sunday.

feed.author: sub-optimal
feed.body:
unpopular: half the CWs on this instance aren't content warnings, they're subject lines with a bit of drama on.

"cw: food" on a picture of a sandwich. "cw: local politics" on the bin collection. "cw: winter" on frost, in a county where it is frost for five months.

a CW is supposed to be for something that hurts people. we've turned it into a table of contents and then got precious about it

replies.author: Audra Speck
replies.body:
Food is a real one. I have two people in my phone who cannot scroll past a plate on a bad day and one of them is my sister.

The bin collection one I will give you.

replies.author: sub-optimal
replies.body: yeah ok. food's a real one. i withdraw food.

replies.author: Corman Betts
replies.body: I put cw winter on it because it is September and it is not funny yet and I wanted people to be able to not look. That is the whole of my reasoning. I am not being precious, I am being a coward about October.

replies.author: Tess Ruddock
replies.body:
The rule says violence, medical, death, food, and politics about people rather than potholes. Everything past that is manners, and I do not moderate manners.

If somebody CWs a sandwich you have lost four pixels and a second. If somebody does not CW the one that mattered, Audra's sister has a bad afternoon. The costs are not the same size and that is the whole argument.

replies.author: Priya Shanbhag
replies.body: Asymmetric costs, so bias toward the cheap error. This instance keeps accidentally doing good engineering and calling it being polite.

feed.author: Ann Sloat
feed.body:
[b]CW: death of an animal, old age, nothing violent[/b]

We lost Pitch this morning. Barn cat, black, seventeen or eighteen, nobody was ever sure because she arrived on her own in the spring of 2009 and never explained herself.

She was in the sun by the step and then she was not breathing, and that is the whole of it, and it is the ending you would pick.

Don looked at the ground by the fence for a long time before he started digging. He is not a man who says things.

She caught one mouse in eighteen years. We saw it happen. She looked as surprised as we did.

replies.author: Audra Speck
replies.body: Oh, Ann.

replies.author: Lissa Vollmer
replies.body: Seventeen years and one mouse. I am going to think about that cat for the rest of my life.

replies.body: I am so sorry. Thank you for the CW, I used it, and then I read it anyway about ten minutes later, which I think is what they are for.

replies.body:
We are so sorry for your loss.

We have created a free memorial page for PITCH. Photos, candles and a guestbook are included. Claim it within 7 days or it will be listed publicly.

replies.body:

Seventeen years and one mouse.

feed.author: Tess Ruddock
feed.body:
Three and a half years, so here are the numbers. Somebody asked and I would rather everyone had them than one person did.

[b]Accounts:[/b] 180 registered. 34 posted in the last 30 days. 11 of those 34 live in Verity County.

So the local timeline is a county board where two thirds of the room have never been to the county. I have made peace with this. You lot ask better questions about the plough budget than anyone who has to pay for it.

[b]Money:[/b] $14 a month for the VPS, $6.40 a month for the media storage, $22 a year for the domain. $266.80 a year. Four people send me $5 a month without being asked and one person sent $50 once in 2024 and I still do not know who it was.

That is more than covered. I am not asking for anything. I am telling you what it costs because I think you should know what things cost.

[b]Time:[/b] about four hours a week. Most of it is spam on a Sunday.

I work IT for the school district. Two buildings, 1,900 kids, a phone system from 2011 that I am not allowed to replace. This is the restful one.

replies.author: Priya Shanbhag
replies.body: You have typed a square bracket instead of a round one in front of Time and it has rendered as literal text and I am not going to be able to stop looking at it.

Ruth I have not asked. Ruth would probably say yes and then post four times in March.

If they want an account it is here and it is free and it takes me two minutes. That is the offer and it does not expire.

feed.author: verityfeed.social
feed.body:
[b]Moderation notice — federation suspended with grandvista.social[/b]

Posting this here because the rules say I post it here.

As of 06:00 this morning verityfeed.social has suspended federation with grandvista.social. This is a suspension and not a limit: no posts in either direction, media purged, and existing follows are severed both ways.

Reason: eleven reports in nine days, all of the same kind, all naming the same four accounts, and no response from their moderation address. I wrote three times. The third one bounced.

If you had followers there, you have lost them, and unsuspending will not bring them back — everyone would have to follow again and in my experience nobody does. I am sorry. There is nothing I can do about that from this end.

The full block list is on the About page and it always has been. There are nine entries on it. Every one of them has a date and a sentence.

— Tess

replies.author: Verity Aldiss
replies.body: Read it. Thank you for writing the reasons down. Most places do not and then act surprised when people invent worse ones.

replies.author: Growth Unlocked
